newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS ATLETICO CRASH TO COMPOSTELA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS ATLETICO CRASH TO COMPOSTELA.

text.p: Titleholders Atletico Madrid slipped up badly when they went down 3-1 to Compostela in the second weekend of the Spanish league season on Saturday.

An Atletico side that clearly missed injured international playmaker Jose Luis Caminero went behind to a Nacho Fernandez goal before coming back to equalise through Juan Eduardo Esnaider on the stroke of half-time.

Esnaider -- who had looked Atletico's most dangerous player -- was substituted by coach Radomir Antic at the break after living up to his volatile reputation by picking up a yellow card for challenging an offside decision.
It was all uphill for Atletico after Czech international Radek Bejbl was sent off for a heavy challenge just five minutes into the second half.

The Compostela forwards, who had seen their team go down 6-0 in the first game of the season, capitalised on the numerical advantage and only fine work by Atletico keeper Jose Molina kept the score down to 3-1.

A last minute strike by Juan Pizzi gave Barcelona a 2-1 victory in an exciting Catalan derby against Espanyol, saving a game that Bobby Robson's side had looked like losing until just seven minutes from time.
Both sides struggled to find their best form in the first half on a Nou Camp pitch that cut up badly throughout the game.
"The surface was good for Barcelona's Brazilians -- they're used to playing on the beach," said Espanyol captain Jordi Lardin after the game.
Lardin had put his side ahead after 70 minutes on the clock after finishing off a four-against-one counterattack.

But Espanyol looked increasingly shaky as Barcelona pushed for an equaliser, and when the defence failed to clear a cross from Hristo Stoichkov, Brazilian midfielder Giovanni was on hand to smash the ball into the roof of the net.
A similar mistake let through Pizzi, and the international forward gave goalkeeper Toni Jimenez no chance.
The result was particularly harsh for Espanyol, who lost last year's game in similar circumstances, after they went down 3-2 to Sporting Gijon in the first game of the season after leading 2-0.
Ahead of Sunday's games surprise outfit Tenerife are the provisional leaders of the Spanish first division after following up their 6-0 victory in the opening match with a 1-0 win at Logrones.
Another unfancied team, Real Sociedad, join Tenerife and Barcelona at the top after bringing home three points from their visit to Valencia thanks to a single goal from Darko Kovacevic.
The result is likely to increase the tension at Valencia, last year's runners-up who have been one of the biggest spenders in the close season.
Club chairman Francisco Roig and coach Luis Aragones had already clashed before the beginning of the season, which began with Valencia losing at Racing Santander after leading 2-0.
